vulnerabilities.description: Memory files stored in .claude-flow/data/ are created with world-readable permissions (rw-rw-r--). Any local user can read session context, exposing sensitive data, API keys, or authentication tokens.
vulnerabilities.impact: Confidentiality breach - local users can access session secrets

vulnerabilities.description: Session files in .claude-flow/sessions/ created with rw-rw-r-- permissions. Group/world readable access to session context, metrics, and workflow information.
vulnerabilities.impact: Confidentiality breach - local privilege escalation or information disclosure

vulnerabilities.description: No input validation on set() function. Arbitrary key-value pairs without sanitization. Attacker could corrupt JSON or exhaust disk space.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of service or JSON parsing errors

vulnerabilities.description: Silent error handling - catch block ignores all errors without logging. Corrupted/truncated JSON returns empty object without alerting user.
vulnerabilities.impact: Silent data loss or inconsistent state

vulnerabilities.description: Race window between temp file write and rename in atomicWrite(). Process crash could leave orphaned temp files. Concurrent writers could collide.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource
vulnerabilities.impact: Temporary file accumulation and potential session corruption

vulnerabilities.description: Temp files cleaned up in finally block. SIGTERM/SIGKILL before cleanup leaves files in /tmp/. No automatic stale file cleanup.
vulnerabilities.impact: Disk space accumulation in /tmp/, exposure of body content

vulnerabilities.description: Hook commands use `sh -c` with unquoted variable interpolation. If CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or HOME contain special characters, command injection possible.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements

vulnerabilities.description: buildPattern() constructs alternation regex without size limits. Malicious task description with many regex chars could cause ReDoS.
vulnerabilities.impact: Denial of service - CPU spike during task routing

vulnerabilities.description: Memory, session, and intelligence data stored in plaintext JSON with group-readable permissions in multiuser environments.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.impact: Confidentiality breach if memory contains API keys or tokens

recommendations: CRITICAL: Fix file permissions - use fs.writeFileSync(file, data, {mode: 0o600}) for memory/session files
CRITICAL: Implement atomic writes in memory.js (copy pattern from session.js with temp file + rename)
HIGH: Add input validation to memory.set() - validate key names, value size limits, JSON schema
HIGH: Quote environment variables in settings.json hook commands to prevent injection: sh -c 'D="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}"; ... exec node "$D/..."'
HIGH: Encrypt memory and session files at rest using TweetNaCl.js or similar
MEDIUM: Replace silent catch blocks with proper error logging to stderr
MEDIUM: Add /tmp cleanup routine for stale gh-body-*.tmp files older than 1 hour
MEDIUM: Add ReDoS protection to router.js - timeout on regex or limit task description to 10KB
LOW: Add JSON schema validation when loading memory/session files
LOW: Document security assumptions (single-user or trusted-user environment)
